subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust lifecycle for generated HTML after outbound staging?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and tested, but it deliberately authorizes a new path for local HTML host-read delivery, so automation should not decide the permanent security boundary alone.

options.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle
options.body: Approve the sha256/size SQLite marker design as the supported boundary for trusted generated HTML after outbound staging.

options.title: Require Tighter Lifecycle First
options.body: Ask for an additional bound such as created_at TTL cleanup or chunked prune handling before accepting the trust expansion.

options.title: Reject Staged HTML Trust
options.body: Keep temp-root-only trust and leave the linked message-loss issue unresolved until a different product/security design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve the sha256/size SQLite marker design as the supported boundary for trusted generated HTML after outbound staging.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the original trusted generated HTML seam and has the clearest history on the intended host-read boundary.
